sights.w: The 65-room Tudor Revival country estate Goodyear co-founder F.A. Seiberling built in 1912–15, with 70 acres of Warren Manning landscapes and an English garden — Akron's grandest house, a National Historic Landmark and the place Alcoholics Anonymous was born (Henrietta Seiberling introduced Bill W. to Dr. Bob in the Gate Lodge, 1935).

sights.address: 2121 George Halas Dr NW, Canton, OH 44708
sights.w: The shrine of American football, opened 1963 in the city where the NFL (as the APFA) was founded at Ralph Hay's Hupmobile showroom in 1920 — busts of every enshrinee in the Hall of Fame Gallery, the Lombardi trophies, and the August enshrinement week that takes over Canton.

NPS site in downtown Canton telling the stories of America's First Ladies: the education & research center in the 1895 City National Bank building and, a block south, the Saxton McKinley House (331 Market Ave S), Ida Saxton McKinley's family home where William and Ida lived.

sights.address: 800 McKinley Monument Dr NW, Canton, OH 44708
sights.w: The domed granite mausoleum (1907) on a hill above Canton where the assassinated 25th president, Ida and their two daughters are entombed — 108 steps up, with a view over the city.

sights.address: 800 McKinley Monument Dr NW, Canton, OH 44708
sights.w: Stark County Historical Society's museum at the foot of the McKinley Memorial: the largest McKinley collection anywhere, a walk-through 'Street of Shops', the Discover World science hall and a planetarium.

Akron's art museum: the 1899 Renaissance Revival former post office joined to Coop Himmelb(l)au's 2007 'Roof Cloud' steel-and-glass Knight Building — modern and contemporary American art, free admission.

sights.n: May 4 Visitors Center (Kent State May 4 Site)
sights.w: Kent State's museum of the May 4, 1970 shootings, when Ohio National Guardsmen killed four students and wounded nine during an anti-war protest — in Taylor Hall beside the 18-acre National Historic Landmark site, with the outdoor walking tour, Prentice Hall lot markers and the Don Drumm 'Solar Totem' bullet hole.
The WPA-built 1936 hill track in southeast Akron where kids in gravity-powered cars have raced the All-American Soap Box Derby world championship every July since 1946.
Compact, well-loved accredited zoo on Perkins Park in west Akron — Komodo dragons, snow leopards, Grizzly Ridge and the Journey to Madagascar building.

Summit Metro Parks' gorge of the Cuyahoga River at the falls the city is named for — the Gorge Trail along sandstone ledges to Mary Campbell Cave ('Old Maid's Kitchen'), where a captive 1759 girl was held, below the High Level Bridge.

Built 1917, the oldest airship base in the world and still the home port of the Goodyear Blimp — 'the Kitty Hawk of lighter-than-air.' No public tours; watch the airships launch from the viewing lot or from across the water at Wingfoot Lake State Park.

John Eberson's 1929 Loew's atmospheric movie palace — a Moorish courtyard under a domed ceiling of twinkling stars and drifting clouds — restored and still Akron's main stage for touring shows and concerts.

Canton's 1926 John Eberson atmospheric theatre (National Register), with a Spanish-courtyard auditorium under a starry sky ceiling and its original Kilgen theatre organ — films, concerts and the Canton Symphony's pops.

sights.address: 1875 E Maple St, North Canton, OH 44720
sights.w: The Hoover family farmhouse in North Canton, now Walsh University's museum of the company that made 'hoover' a verb — free guided tours through a collection of antique vacuum cleaners and the town's company history.

Small state park of Sharon-conglomerate ledges in northeast Portage County — squeeze-through crevices (Fat Man's Peril, Devil's Icebox), Cascade and Minnehaha falls, and a newer glass-bottom overlook.

Massillon's shrine to 'Tigertown' football — a 30-foot timeline of Massillon Tiger history from 1891, the early pro Massillon Tigers, and Paul Brown, who coached here before Ohio State, the Browns and the Bengals. Paul Brown Tiger Stadium, Ohio's largest high-school field, is across town.

sights.n: St. Helena III Canal Boat (Canal Fulton)
sights.w: Horse-drawn canal-boat rides on a watered stretch of the original Ohio & Erie Canal — two draft horses tow the St. Helena III about an hour past the McLaughlin dry dock to the Lock IV turning basin, with a historian aboard.
1820s farmhouse of Quakers Thomas and Charity Rotch, a verified NPS Network to Freedom Underground Railroad station — with the secret staircase used to move freedom seekers through the house.

The 1929 airship hangar beside Akron Fulton airport — at completion the largest building in the world without interior supports, big enough to make its own indoor weather; it built the Navy's Akron and Macon. Seen from outside (private).

sights.address: Main St (OH-91) & Aurora St, Hudson, OH 44236
sights.w: A New England village transplanted to the Western Reserve: Greek Revival and Federal houses around the green and James Ellsworth's 1912 clock tower, with Western Reserve Academy ('the Yale of the West') and its 1838 Loomis Observatory a short walk away.

sights.address: Cascade Locks Park, N Howard St, Akron, OH 44308
sights.w: The staircase of seven Ohio & Erie Canal locks that lifted boats 70 ft to the Akron Summit, the canal's highest point; the restored c.1847 Mustill Store at Lock 15 is now a seasonal canal museum on the Towpath Trail.

sights.n: Perkins Stone Mansion & John Brown House
sights.w: Summit County Historical Society's two houses on Akron's west side: Col. Simon Perkins's 1837 Greek Revival stone mansion, and across the road the c.1830 house abolitionist John Brown rented from Perkins in 1844–54 while they ran a sheep and wool partnership.

sights.address: Glendale Ave & S Walnut St, Akron, OH 44302
sights.w: 242 hand-dressed sandstone steps the WPA laid in 1936–37 up a 200-ft slope — Gertrude Seiberling's idea, designed by Warren Manning — a Depression-era monument in a city the rubber layoffs hit hard.
Summit Metro Parks' nature-study preserve on land Goodyear founder F.A. Seiberling owned — the park district's first nature center, a rock garden, ponds and a suspension bridge over the ravine.
